text: The small curd cubes are washed in damp cellars, often at first and then weekly, so local smear ferments form a brown, slightly rosy rind. Ripening runs inward from that rind, leaving the paste more unctuous and mature under it than at the centre.

steps.note: The curd is pressed lightly, between wooden planks.
The curd is cut into cubes of 50–400 g.
The cheese ripens in damp cellars, and is washed 2–3 times a week for the first two weeks, then weekly.
